newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON MAKES NO MISTAKE IN 400 METRES SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON MAKES NO MISTAKE IN 400 METRES SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Double Olympic champion Michael Johnson made no mistake clinching a place in the final of the 400 metres on Monday after almost crashing out in an earlier round because of a badly-judged finish.
The American defending champion set a fast pace in the first 300 metres before easing off in the home straight to win his semifinal in 44.37 seconds and move comfortably into Tuesday's final.

Compatriot Jerome Young, Uganda's Olympic bronze medallist Davis Kamoga and Britain's Iwan Thomas finished second, third and fourth respectively to take the other places in the final from the second heat.

Johnson was almost eliminated in the second round on Sunday after he misjudged the final metres of a heat and failed to qualify directly for the next round as one of the top three finishers. The American scraped through as one of the four fastest losers.
"It felt good," he said on Monday. "I do not have a problem, I did not have a problem yesterday. I just made a mistake and I am very disappointed with myself for doing that but it happened.
"I am ready to go out there and do the best I can to win the race."

American Tyree Washington won a tight finish to the first heat in 44.61 and immediately started boxing the air in celebration after the finish. Britain's Mark Richardson, Jamie Baulch and American Antonio Pettigrew took the other places in the final.
Washington said was not concerned about Johnson who has struggled with injury this season.
"I do not fear the man. He's human," he said.
Johnson was allowed to compete in Athens after the world governing body decided to give automatic entry to defending champions.
The 200 and 400 world champion was not selected for the U.S. team after failing to compete in the national trials because of an injury to his left quadriceps.
